definitions.rationale: This is the empty-sequence base equation defining advanceIndex.
This is the structurally recursive cons equation defining advanceIndex by incrementing the index once per element.
definitions.text:
rule advanceIndex(I:Int, vCons(_:Val, VS:ValSeq))
    => advanceIndex(I +Int 1, VS)

definitions.rationale: This is the empty-sequence base equation defining the scanAppend summary.
This simplification rule is the guarded matching-element recurrence of scanAppend: it appends the current coordinate and recurses on the tail.
definitions.text:
rule scanAppend(ACC:ValSeq, vCons(V:Val, VS:ValSeq),
                  X:Int, RI:Int, CI:Int)
    => scanAppend(
         valSeqConcat(
           ACC,
           vCons(tuple(vCons(RI, vCons(CI, .ValSeq))), .ValSeq)),
         VS, X, RI, CI +Int 1)
    requires V ==K X
    [simplification]

definitions.rationale: This simplification rule is the complementary nonmatching-element recurrence of scanAppend and recurses on the tail without appending.
definitions.text:
rule scanAppend(ACC:ValSeq, vCons(V:Val, VS:ValSeq),
                  X:Int, RI:Int, CI:Int)
    => scanAppend(ACC, VS, X, RI, CI +Int 1)
    requires notBool (V ==K X)
    [simplification]

definitions.rationale: This is the empty-row-sequence base equation defining the rowsAppend summary.
This simplification rule is the guarded recursive rowsAppend equation, defining one row through scanAppend before descending to the remaining rows.
definitions.text:
rule rowsAppend(ACC:ValSeq,
                  vCons(V:Val, RS:ValSeq),
                  X:Int, RI:Int)
    => rowsAppend(scanAppend(ACC, rowContents(V), X, RI, 0),
                  RS, X, RI +Int 1)
    requires V ==K list(rowContents(V))
    [simplification]

definitions.rationale: This macro-expansion equation defines INNERBODY as the exact inner-loop statement constructors.
definitions.text:
rule INNERBODY
    => If(Compare(Name("value"),
                  CmpOp("in", TupleExpr((Name("x"), .Exprs)))),
          Expr(Call(Attribute(Name("coordinates"), "append"),
                    (TupleExpr((Name("row_index"), Name("column_index"), .Exprs)),
                     .Exprs)))
          .Stmts,
          .Stmts)
       AugAssign(Name("column_index"), "+", Int(1))
       .Stmts

definitions.rationale: This macro-expansion equation defines OUTERBODY as the exact outer-loop statement constructors.
definitions.text:
rule OUTERBODY
    => Assign(Name("column_index"), Int(0))
       Assign(Name("value"), Int(0))
       For(Name("value"), Name("row"), INNERBODY)
       AugAssign(Name("row_index"), "+", Int(1))
       .Stmts

definitions.rationale: This macro-expansion equation defines GETROWBODY as the exact target-function statement constructors.
definitions.text:
rule GETROWBODY
    => Assign(Name("coordinates"), ListExpr(.Exprs))
       Assign(Name("row_index"), Int(0))
       Assign(Name("row"), NoneVal)
       Assign(Name("column_index"), Int(0))
       Assign(Name("value"), Int(0))
       For(Name("row"), Name("lst"), OUTERBODY)
       Assign(Name("coordinates"),
              Call(Name("sorted"),
                   (Name("coordinates"),
                    KwArg("key", Name("_column_desc")),
                    .Exprs)))
       Return(Call(Name("sorted"),
                   (Name("coordinates"),
                    KwArg("key", Name("_row_asc")),
                    .Exprs)))
       .Stmts

definitions.rationale: This macro-expansion equation defines COLUMNCLOSURE as the named proof term for the supplied column-key closure.
definitions.text:
rule COLUMNCLOSURE
    => closureVal(("coordinate", .ParamNames),
                  Return(UnaryOp("-", Subscript(Name("coordinate"), Int(1))))
                  .Stmts,
                  0)

definitions.rationale: This macro-expansion equation defines ROWCLOSURE as the named proof term for the supplied row-key closure.

proved_derived_lemmas.rationale: The exact For-to-#loop rewrite and guard are first proved by SHAPE-CONNECTION-SPEC.for-list-shape against SHAPE-CONNECTION, which imports ROW-MODEL and not VERIFICATION; prove.sh runs that #Top proof before compiling the verification module containing this reusable priority rule.
proved_derived_lemmas.text:
rule <k> For(T:Expr, V:Val, B:Stmts)
        => #loop(list(rowContents(V)), T, B) ... </k>
       requires V ==K list(rowContents(V))
       [priority(40)]
